reasoning: Roofline reports compute SOL 41.8% and memory SOL 36.5%, both well below 60%, with 58.2% headroom and not at roofline. This indicates performance is limited by execution inefficiencies (instruction mix/tiling/latency effects) rather than pure bandwidth or raw ALU throughput limits.

root_causes.cause: Non-tensor-core/vector FMA execution path leaves large compute headroom on MI300X.

evidence.interpretation: No tensor-core/MFMA utilization; matrix math is not using highest-throughput matrix units.

fixes.fix: Retune kernel to force MFMA-friendly matmul configs (dtype-specific BLOCK_K/BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N and matrix_instr_nonkdim choices) and validate generated ISA uses matrix instructions.
fixes.rationale: Activating matrix units on CDNA3 substantially increases effective compute throughput and can move compute SOL closer to peak.

root_causes.cause: Memory subsystem is only moderately used despite full warp activity, implying latency/tiling inefficiency rather than bandwidth saturation.

evidence.interpretation: HBM bandwidth is far from saturated, so kernel likely spends cycles in non-bandwidth-limited stalls or inefficient data reuse.

fixes.fix: Increase data reuse and pipeline depth by autotuning larger reuse-oriented tiles and num_stages (e.g., higher BLOCK_K or stages where occupancy allows), while keeping occupancy healthy.
fixes.rationale: Better blocking/prefetch overlap reduces memory-latency exposure and raises both compute and memory utilization.
